task:
FINDER F4c: MODE- AND REFERENCE-SAFE SAVED SURFACES. Start from current main (F4b merged as #965, commit 3fd8e719; the Planner S5b merged as #967). This is the next increment of docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-10-v3-finder-f4-archetype-ui-design.md. Read the whole of its section "PR F4c — mode- and reference-safe saved surfaces" first, plus the F4b behaviour it builds on (sections on Compare, Watchlist and the F4b temporary distance suppression), and implement exactly that contract. Everything stays behind the default-off VITE_FINDER_F4_ENABLED flag: with the flag off, the saved surfaces must behave exactly as on main.

THE CONTRACT, IN SHORT (the design text governs if this summary differs):
1. Replace Compare's duplicated and underscore-derived archetype labels with the canonical F4 metadata (apps/web/src/lib/features/explore/archetypes.ts). Keep historical unknown keys readable as fallbacks; never pretend they are V3 keys.
2. Remove Compare's own browser-side tier thresholds and mapping (compare-metrics.ts). Show a tier only from the corresponding API field.
3. Persist overall potential alongside the selected-fit identity (archetype key and its score) in saved snapshots (storage.ts, shortlist.ts). Compare overall potential across modes. Compare selected fits only between snapshots saved for the same archetype. Compare distances only between snapshots with one exact, identical reference, and label the distance with that reference.
4. Referenced snapshots accept every finite distance, including 0. A legacy snapshot without a reference stays "unknown" and a zero there is never treated as a real distance. Add the design's regression: same-reference distances 0 and a positive value render "0.00 LY" with 0 as the best, while a no-reference legacy zero cannot make the row eligible. This replaces the positive-only behaviour the design cites.
5. Existing saved data in users' browsers must keep loading. Treat old snapshots as unknown mode/reference rather than guessing, and never drop or rewrite them destructively. Cover loading a pre-F4c snapshot in storage tests.
6. Only when all of the above is in place, remove F4b's temporary suppression of the distance metric from the Compare table and CSV in flag-on builds.

FILES. The design's exact list: compare-metrics.ts (+ test), persistence/storage.ts (+ test), shortlist.ts (+ test), ComparePanel.svelte (+ test), WatchlistPanel.svelte (+ test). If something else must change, keep it minimal and say why in your report. Do not touch the API, SQL, workflows or the Dockerfile.

TESTS AND DOCS. Focused Vitest/component tests for every rule above, with the flag on and off. Update apps/web/cypress/e2e/product-journey.cy.ts only if a Compare/Watchlist step there needs it, keeping its waits' explicit request windows. Add a dated CHANGES.md entry, and a short dated status line in section 1 of the F4 design saying F4c is implemented (not "on a branch"), and that F4e, browser and visual acceptance, the owner's enablement decision (question 3) and the governed release still remain before the flag may be enabled.

VALIDATION before you finish, and report each result:
- apps/web: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm check`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm build`, eslint and prettier on touched files.
- The whole database-free Python suite, because contract tests read web files: `python -m pytest -q tests/ --ignore=tests/integration --ignore=tests/test_v3_spatial_pyramid.py --ignore=tests/test_admin_cache_truthfulness.py --ignore=tests/test_journal_commander_association.py` (tests that need PostgreSQL skip without a database URL). It must have no failures; report the counts.
- `grep -rln "@babylonjs/" apps/web/src | grep -v "lib/spatial/babylon/"` must print nothing.
